message.content:
Below are two ways you can create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **RTX A6000 GPU** and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Important** – The RTX A6000 is only available in a handful of zones (e.g. `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`).  
> Make sure you pick a zone that supports the `A6000` GPU family.

---

## 1️⃣  Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1. Pick a zone that offers the RTX A6000
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2. Create a new VM instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
    --zone=${ZONE} \
    --machine-type=n1-highmem-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 61 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --metadata=startup-script='#!/bin/bash
        apt-get update && apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
        reboot' \
    --guest-accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --reservation-affinity=any
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--zone` | Where the instance lives (must support A6000) |
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM size (pick one that fits your workload) |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--guest-accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--metadata=startup-script` | Installs NVIDIA drivers automatically |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs, change `count=1` to the desired number (max 8 per instance).

---

## 2️⃣  Using the REST API (JSON body)

If you prefer to use the REST API directly (or via Terraform / Pulumi), here’s a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine Instances endpoint:

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-highmem-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100
      },
      "autoDelete": true,
      "type": "PERSISTENT"
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update && apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535\nreboot"
      }
    ]
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/project-id/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ]
}
```

### How to POST it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/your-project-id/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace:

* `project-id` with your actual GCP project ID.
* `@instance.json` with the path to the JSON file containing the payload above.

---

## 🎯 Quick Checklist

1. **Zone** – Verify the zone supports `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="name:nvidia-tesla-a6000" --format="table(name,zone)"
   ```
2. **Quota** – Ensure you have enough GPU quota in that zone.  
   ```bash
   gcloud compute accelerator-types describe nvidia-tesla-a6000 --zone=us-central1-a
   ```
3. **Billing** – GPU usage incurs extra charges. Check your budget.

Once the instance is running, SSH into it and verify the driver:

```bash
ssh my-rtx-a6000
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version. Happy GPU computing!
